An operation is idempotent when repeating the same request has the same intended effect as making it once. This does not mean that every detail stays the same. Repeated requests can still create additional log entries.

For example, suppose you submit a payment request with an idempotency key, then repeat the same request with the same key. While the stored result is available, this hypothetical payment API does not create another charge. The intended effect is one charge, even though you sent the request twice. Each request may still add a log entry.

In this API, the stored result expires after 24 hours. After expiry, the same key is treated as new, so you should not rely on it to prevent another charge at that point.

Authorization is a separate requirement. Idempotency controls the intended effect of repeating a request. It does not, by itself, guarantee that the request is authorized.
